name: Quantum error correction and fault tolerance
summary: Quantum codes and the threshold theorem showed reliable quantum computation is possible with noisy gates.

name: Motivic integration
summary: Measures on arc spaces are valued in a Grothendieck ring of varieties, generalising p-adic integration with model-theoretic tools.

name: Floer homology with Morava K-theory proves Arnold conjecture over any ring
summary: Floer's orbit-counting method was combined with chromatic homotopy theory to count fixed points of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms using generalised cohomology, proving Arnold's conjecture in cases classical Floer theory could not reach.

name: Feynman periods and motives
summary: Particle-collision amplitudes were found to be periods of motives, and not all are multiple zeta values, prompting a search for an underlying Galois-type symmetry.

name: Stability theory in diophantine geometry (Hrushovski)
summary: Stability-theoretic results about definable groups prove the Mordell-Lang conjecture for function fields and give a model-theoretic proof of Manin-Mumford.

name: A^1-homotopy theory and motivic cohomology
summary: Homotopy theory is rebuilt over schemes with the affine line as the interval, giving motivic cohomology and the proof of the Milnor conjecture.

name: SYZ conjecture
summary: Mirror pairs were conjectured to be dual special Lagrangian torus fibrations, giving a geometric picture of mirror symmetry.

name: Learning with errors and lattice cryptography
summary: Regev's LWE gave worst-case to average-case reductions and a quantum reduction from lattice problems.

name: Deformation quantization of Poisson manifolds
summary: The passage from classical to quantum observables is solved for every Poisson manifold by a formality theorem using string-theory-inspired graph integrals.

name: Kitaev's topological quantum computation
from: topological quantum field theory / modular tensor categories
summary: Fault-tolerant quantum computation by anyons used modular tensor categories and links to Jones-type invariants.
